title: Top-account intake timebox allocation and cross-team capacity swaps
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers with escalations often need guaranteed delivery windows. Our existing intake prioritization is score-based but lacks a deterministic timebox and a mechanism for swapping committed delivery slots across teams when capacity shifts. This ticket proposes a 'timebox allocation' pattern paired with a cross-team capacity swap policy to improve predictability for top accounts and reduce manual escalations.

Proposal: 1) Allocate short, firm delivery windows (timeboxes) for top-account intake items at the point of acceptance (e.g., 2-week, 4-week, 8-week buckets). 2) Maintain a team-level 'swap ledger' that allows teams to exchange portioned capacity credits to honor commitments without overcommitting individual squads. 3) Introduce guardrails: swap limits per sprint, mandatory engineering acceptance for any swap impacting core platform work, and automatic rollback triggers if latency/cost SLOs degrade.

Trade-offs considered: - Strict timeboxes improve customer certainty but reduce scheduling flexibility. - Credit swaps introduce operational complexity and need a lightweight UI in Console. - Automating swaps vs manual approvals: start manual with telemetry-driven suggestions.

Outcomes: More predictable commitments to top accounts, fewer ad hoc escalations, measurable reduction in severity-2 account incidents tied to delivery slippage.
acceptance_criteria: Timebox UI in intake form created in Console and exposed to PMs (mockups approved).
Swap ledger mechanics documented and a first-pass API spec available in Confluence.
Pilot with 3 strategic accounts and two engineering squads completed without SLO regressions.
Metrics dashboard shows reduction in 'delivery-slippage' for pilot accounts by >= 30% after 8 weeks.
